# Results — Study 87 (Center-Line) on real 5-minute tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — fade price
deviations from the running session VWAP by more than **1 ATR(20)**, enter at the next
bar's open in the *opposite* direction, exit on symmetric ±1 ATR barriers, flat at the
16:00 ET close — run across a basket of eight liquid instruments and pinned against a
**random-direction control** on the *same* entries. RTH 09:30–16:00 ET. As-of
**2026-06-12**; Yahoo serves only ~60 calendar days of 5-minute bars, so the window is a
rolling span ending ~now — match the per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold the same
tape. Trades pooled across the basket: **n = 23,462** (~48.9 trades/instrument/day).*

## The honest test — symmetric ±1 ATR, gross (cost = 0, threshold = 1.0 ATR deviation)

A direction-symmetric payoff is the only fair way to ask *"does the VWAP-deviation signal
point the right way?"* — with TP and SL equidistant, a coin earns ≈ 0.

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **VWAP fade (against deviation)** | 23,462 | **49.2%** | **−0.35** | **−1.16** |
| Random direction (control) | 23,462 | 49.1% | −0.25 | −1.69 |

- The VWAP-fade's gross expectancy is **−0.35 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **−1.16** —
  statistically **indistinguishable from zero**, slightly negative.
- It does **not beat the coin.** Fade − random = **−0.09 bps/trade**; the signal adds
  essentially nothing over a random-direction entry on identical bars.
- The bootstrap 95% CI on the annualised Sharpe is **[−4.67, +1.42]** (86% of resamples
  negative), confirming no detectable edge.
- Per-instrument, no tape carries a real edge: every HAC |*t*| ≤ 1.25 (SPY −0.71,
  QQQ −0.62, IWM −0.33, AAPL −0.48, TSLA −1.25, NVDA +0.40, ES −0.74, NQ −0.29).

## Threshold sweep — no threshold unlocks an edge

We tested 0.5 ATR (mild), 1.0 ATR (moderate), and 2.0 ATR (aggressive) deviation thresholds
to check whether a sharper entry buys a better signal. None do:

| Threshold | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.5 ATR (mild) | 29,136 | 49.3% | −0.35 | −1.27 |
| 1.0 ATR (moderate) | 23,462 | 49.2% | −0.35 | −1.16 |
| 2.0 ATR (aggressive) | 14,287 | 48.6% | −0.60 | −1.68 |

A higher threshold reduces the trade count but does not improve the mean return. The
VWAP-fade's win-rate and expectancy are flat to negative across all thresholds.

## Could you trade it? — the cost sweep

At ~**48.9 trades/instrument/day** (12,318/yr), the gross negative edge is destroyed by any
cost. The **gross is already negative**, so there is **no positive break-even cost**:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | ann. P&L |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −0.35 | −1.16 | −42.7%/yr |
| 0.5 bps | −0.85 | **−2.83** | — |
| 1.0 bps | −1.35 | **−4.49** | **−166%/yr** |
| 2.0 bps | −2.35 | −7.83 | — |

At ~49 trades/day the break-even is undefined — the strategy was never alive. Even a 0.5 bp
round-trip earns a HAC *t* of −2.83, certifying it as a significant loser.

## The mechanical mean-reversion problem

The large trade count (~49/day/ticker) is the structural tell: price is near the VWAP *most
of the time* already (by definition, VWAP is the average), so the 1-ATR threshold is crossed
frequently by normal noise, not extreme dislocations. These are not overshoots waiting to
snap back — they are ordinary noise bars masquerading as mean-reversion signals. The real
mean-reversion is purely mechanical (the VWAP is a moving average of the price; by
construction, price is usually close to it) and offers nothing tradable.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Gross HAC *t* = −1.16 (sign slightly wrong), no edge over a
  random-direction control (Δ = −0.09 bps), every instrument |*t*| ≤ 1.25, no threshold
  unlocks a signal. Intraday mean-reversion to VWAP is mechanical — not a forecastable edge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Negative gross expectancy at ~49 trades/day → a significant
  loser at any realistic cost (*t* = −4.49 at 1 bp), ≈ −166%/yr net. No positive
  break-even cost exists.
- **Beats a coin? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The "price always returns to VWAP" fade does not beat
  a coin on a symmetric test. The VWAP is a centre of mass by construction; mean-reversion
  toward it is an accounting identity, not a tradable signal.
